summary: Design and adversarially review the remaining WebSocket fast-lane and live-proof fixes

result.summary:
The defect is real and the fix should ship. On origin/main, `classify_disconnect` (crates/core/src/websocket/pool_supervisor.rs:757) puts 808 in the same Fatal arm as 806 and 810. That arm calls `park(ParkReason::FatalDisconnect)`, and `allows_one_respawn` is false for it, so a single 808 leaves the slot dark for the whole session. 807 and 809 refresh the token and redial instead (TokenStale arm, ~2950). Verified. The order side already handles 808 by refreshing and retrying once (oms/error_taxonomy.rs maps Data808 to TokenRefreshRetryOnce). Verified by review. connection.rs only decodes the code; the policy lives in pool_supervisor.rs alone.

This final spec keeps the design's shape: one shared, floored, jittered refresh-then-redial for a first 808, and a session park only after a fresh token is also rejected. 806 and 810 stay fatal on the first strike; 805 and ROTATION_HALTED are untouched. Review findings folded in:

(1) "Fresh" is now tied to WHICH token was verified. The token manager's `renew_generation` goes up on every token install (Verified at the acquire, renew, SSM-adopt and cache-adopt sites). The refresh closure already records the generation each dial presented (`dialled_generation`). So the slot parks only when the dial that got 808 presented the exact generation that an earlier refresh produced. This removes the stale `fresh_verified` problem across DialFailed loops, transient closes, 805 parks and probe releases, and later forced re-mints.

(2) A refusal because of the mint cooldown or RESILIENCE-03 is reported as `Deferred` and does not count toward the cap. A wall-clock limit on the whole episode (at least 2 × the 125 s mint cooldown) is the backstop. Without this, all 16 slots would park within about 20 s, while a mint would still have been refused for another ~100 s.

(3) A stacked `[data][808]` frame no longer clears the episode, because nothing on the frame path changes any more. The episode ends only when the credential has proven itself: a non-808 close after frames, or an 808 that arrives after at least MIN_HEALTHY_SESSION_MS of healthy delivery. So the first-frame edit, the hot-path edit and the DHAT concern are all gone.

(4) The 4-refreshes-per-session limit is replaced by a 4-per-300 s window, kept in a fixed `Copy` ring of timestamps.

(5) A failed renewal is now shared across sockets for 10 s. Before, coalescing only worked on success: 16 sockets with a dead token could each send their own failing RenewToken call. That also cuts the 807 path's auth-call burst.

(6) The freshness signal is the generation, not `expires_at`. The design wrongly assumed `expires_at` is the JWT exp (it is only on the SSM-adopt path), and the "re-adopts the same token from SSM" risk does not apply: the fallback is a fresh mint. Both points are dropped.

(7) The process blocker is fixed. origin/main already has exactly 5 active plans, the V7 cap, so the work goes into the existing IN_PROGRESS active-plan-feed-hardening.md rather than a 6th file.

(8) The missed guards and docs are added: the exact `ReconnectReason::ALL` label pin in `no_deliberate_redial_remains_for_a_subscription_change`, the two terraform alarm descriptions that say 808 parks permanently, AUTH-GAP-02 and the AuthGapDisconnectTokenMap doc, and the extra stale comments.

(9) For the depth account, an 808 refresh may only re-read its own SSM token, never call RenewToken or mint. A second token issuer for that account would break §10.4 and §10.9 of the minter rule.

(10) The noise-lock row now says honestly that a self-healing 808 can still fire the existing `dhan-main-reconnect-slow` alarm, exactly as 807 can.

Dropped as invalid or out of scope: the `From<()>` shortcut (it would let a production closure report a fresh token by default, a false OK); clearing the episode on the first frame (fails on stacked frames); using `Data808AuthFailed` as a new emit site (it could trip the code-coverage guards for no gain); and skipping renewal when sibling sockets are still delivering (no shared per-generation delivery signal exists, and 809 already renews on a single-socket rejection). That last one is recorded as a residual risk.

Hot path: no change per frame or per tick. Every new branch runs on the disconnect path or the refresh path, which are O(1), allocation-free and use `Copy` state.

STEP 0. Rule files and plan, in the same PR as the code (rule-file-first)
0a. docs/claude-rules-full/project/websocket-connection-scope-lock.md
- Append after the last 2026-10-02 section: `### 2026-10-06 — 808 REFRESHES THE TOKEN ONCE BEFORE IT PARKS`.
- Quote the operator verbatim: "Go ahead with whatever you want dude" and "See do everything whatever is recommended dude okay?" (2026-10-06).
- Contract: a first 808 triggers ONE shared token refresh and a redial with floor and jitter (same delay rule as 807). The slot parks for the session (FatalDisconnect, no 804 respawn) only when one of these holds:
  - (a) the dial that got 808 presented the token generation that an earlier refresh in the same episode produced;
  - (b) AUTH_REJECT_MAX_HARD_FAILURES refreshes failed outright;
  - (c) the episode is older than AUTH_REJECT_EPISODE_MAX_MS without a verified fresh token;
  - (d) more than AUTH_REJECT_MAX_REFRESHES_PER_WINDOW refreshes happened inside AUTH_REJECT_WINDOW_MS.
  806 and 810 stay fatal on the first strike. 805 and ROTATION_HALTED are unchanged. Refresh is per account.
- Depth account: an 808 on a depth-account socket may only RE-READ `/tickvault/<env>/dhan-depth/access-token`. It never calls RenewToken or generateAccessToken, and never calls `global_token_manager()`.
- Out of scope, stated: a rejection at the HTTP upgrade arrives as DialFailed. That path does not refresh, and this change does not alter it.
- The new reconnect reason label `auth_rejected` is authorised here.
- REJECT rows:
  - retrying an 808 without a refresh;
  - redialling below TOKEN_STALE_REDIAL_FLOOR_MS;
  - raising any AUTH_REJECT_* cap without a dated quote;
  - making 806 or 810 refreshable;
  - spending the 804 respawn budget on 808;
  - setting or clearing ROTATION_HALTED on 808;
  - an 808 on one account refreshing another account's token;
  - a depth-account 808 calling RenewToken or a mint;
  - a production refresh closure that reports `Fresh` without the generation having moved;
  - clearing the episode on the frame path.

STEP 1. pool_supervisor.rs: classification
- Add `DisconnectClass::AuthRejected`, documented as "808, ambiguous: an invalid token or an invalid client id; refresh once, park on a second rejection of a fresh token".
- In `classify_disconnect`, remove `DisconnectCode::AuthenticationFailed` from the Fatal arm and add `Some(DisconnectCode::AuthenticationFailed) => DisconnectClass::AuthRejected`.
- Update the docs and comments that say 808 is fatal: the `DisconnectClass::Fatal` doc, the `ParkReason::FatalDisconnect` doc, the `allows_one_respawn` doc and its inline comment, the `TOKEN_STALE_REDIAL_FLOOR_MS` doc ("807/808/809"), the `SupervisorAction::RefreshTokenThenDial` doc, the inline "Credential/entitlement (806/808/810)" comment (~2361), and the Fatal-arm log text (say 806/810, or 808 after a failed refresh).
- `ParkReason` keeps four variants. `allows_one_respawn(FatalDisconnect)` stays false.

STEP 2. pool_supervisor.rs: new public types and constants
```rust
pub const AUTH_REJECT_MAX_HARD_FAILURES: u8 = 3;
pub const AUTH_REJECT_EPISODE_MAX_MS: u64 = 300_000; // const assert >= 2 * DHAN_TOKEN_GENERATION_COOLDOWN_SECS * 1000
pub const AUTH_REJECT_WINDOW_MS: u64 = 300_000;
pub const AUTH_REJECT_MAX_REFRESHES_PER_WINDOW: usize = 4;
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct TokenRefreshRequest { pub skip_if_presented: Option<u64> }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub enum TokenRefreshOutcome { Fresh { current: u64 }, Deferred, Failed, NotAttempted }
#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)] pub struct TokenRefreshReport { pub presented: u64, pub outcome: TokenRefreshOutcome }
```
- Private: `#[derive(Clone, Copy)] struct AuthRejectEpisode { started_at: Instant, hard_failures: u8, verified_generation: Option<u64> }`.
- New `ConnectionSupervisor` fields: `auth_reject: Option<AuthRejectEpisode>` (None at start) and `auth_reject_refreshes: [Option<Instant>; AUTH_REJECT_MAX_REFRESHES_PER_WINDOW]`, a ring with a `u8` cursor.
- `const _: () = assert!(AUTH_REJECT_EPISODE_MAX_MS >= 2 * DHAN_TOKEN_GENERATION_COOLDOWN_SECS * 1000);`

STEP 3. pool_supervisor.rs: shared delay helper
- Extract `fn token_floor_delay(&mut self, now: Instant) -> (u64, FlapVerdict)`. It returns `(damped.delay_ms.max(TOKEN_STALE_REDIAL_FLOOR_MS).saturating_add(self.jitter_ms()), damped.verdict)`, keeping the existing 2026-08-11 / 2026-08-19 comment block.
- The TokenStale arm calls it. Its behaviour must stay byte-identical.

STEP 4. pool_supervisor.rs: the `DisconnectClass::AuthRejected` arm in `on_event(ConnEvent::Disconnected)`
- (a) If `self.auth_reject.is_some()` and `self.healthy_duration_ms(now) >= MIN_HEALTHY_SESSION_MS`, set `self.auth_reject = None`. The credential was accepted on this dial.
- (b) If the episode is None, start one: `Some(AuthRejectEpisode { started_at: now, hard_failures: 0, verified_generation: None })`.
- (c) If every ring slot is Some and the oldest is within AUTH_REJECT_WINDOW_MS of `now`: log `error!(code = ErrorCode::WsGapDisconnectClassification.code_str(), stage = "parked_refresh_ceiling", disconnect_code = 808u16, endpoint, pool_index, ...)`, then `return self.park(ParkReason::FatalDisconnect, now)`.
- (d) If `hard_failures >= AUTH_REJECT_MAX_HARD_FAILURES`, or (`verified_generation.is_none()` and the episode age is at least AUTH_REJECT_EPISODE_MAX_MS): log the same way with `stage = "parked_refresh_unavailable"`, then park.
- (e) Otherwise:
  - write `now` into the ring;
  - log `error!(code = WsGapDisconnectClassification, stage = "refresh_then_redial", disconnect_code = 808u16, ...)`;
  - `let (delay, verdict) = self.token_floor_delay(now);`
  - `self.enter_backoff(ReconnectReason::AuthRejected, verdict, now);`
  - return `SupervisorAction::RefreshTokenThenDial { delay_ms: delay }`.
- This arm never touches ROTATION_HALTED. `overflow_episode_note_disconnect` already ignores Some(808) (Verified).

STEP 5. pool_supervisor.rs: when an episode ends
- At the top of `enter_backoff`: `if self.proven_healthy && reason != ReconnectReason::AuthRejected { self.auth_reject = None; }`. A non-808 close after frames proves the credential. This is cold code and runs before `proven_healthy` is reset.
- In `park()`: set `self.auth_reject = None` for every reason. A PoolOverflow park that is later released by the probe starts clean.
- NOTHING changes in the `FrameReceived` arm.
- Re-run the source pins that slice `fn enter_backoff(` and `fn park(&mut self, reason: ParkReason` (~10043, ~11899, ~17260). Keep any substring they pin, and extend them only if needed.

STEP 6. pool_supervisor.rs: the refresh interface
- `pub fn token_refresh_request(&self) -> TokenRefreshRequest` returns `{ skip_if_presented: self.auth_reject.and_then(|e| e.verified_generation) }`.
- `pub fn note_token_refresh(&mut self, report: TokenRefreshReport, now: Instant) -> Option<SupervisorAction>` behaves as follows:
  - No episode: return None. 807 and 809 are unchanged.
  - If `episode.verified_generation == Some(report.presented)`: log `error!(code = WsGapDisconnectClassification, stage = "parked_fresh_token_rejected", presented_generation = report.presented, ...)` and return `Some(self.park(ParkReason::FatalDisconnect, now))`.
  - Otherwise, by outcome:
    - Fresh{current} sets `verified_generation = Some(current)`;
    - Deferred changes nothing;
    - Failed and NotAttempted do `hard_failures = hard_failures.saturating_add(1)`.
    Then return None.
- Change the bounds on `run_connection` (~6878) and `run_connection_with_commands` (~7034) to `F: FnMut(TokenRefreshRequest) -> Fut, Fut: Future<Output = TokenRefreshReport>`. Do NOT add `From<()>`.
- In the shell's `RefreshTokenThenDial` arm (~7156), replace `if !sink.stop_requested() { refresh_token().await; } action = supervisor.on_event(ConnEvent::BeginDial, Instant::now());` with:
```rust
let mut parked = None;
if !sink.stop_requested() {
    let report = refresh_token(supervisor.token_refresh_request()).await;
    parked = supervisor.note_token_refresh(report, Instant::now());
}
action = match parked { Some(a) => a, None => supervisor.on_event(ConnEvent::BeginDial, Instant::now()) };
```
  The loop's existing Park arm produces `ConnectionExit::Parked(FatalDisconnect)`.

STEP 7. pool_supervisor.rs: metrics and labels
- Add `ReconnectReason::AuthRejected`: `as_str` = "auth_rejected", included in `ALL` (`[Self; 7]` becomes `[Self; 8]`, appended last), `records_flap` = true.
- The existing pre-registration loop zero-registers `tv_dhan_ws_reconnect_total{reason="auth_rejected"}`.
- The terminal park reuses PARK_METRIC `reason="fatal_disconnect"`.

STEP 8. token_manager.rs (crates/core/src/auth)
- 8a. Add `#[must_use] pub fn is_deferred_renewal_failure(err: &ApplicationError) -> bool`. It is true for `AuthenticationFailed` whose reason starts with MINT_COOLDOWN_REFUSAL_REASON_PREFIX or RESILIENCE03_MINT_REFUSAL_REASON_PREFIX. Refactor `stale_credential_failure_pages` to call it, so there is one classifier.
- 8b. Failure reuse. Add the constant `RENEW_FAILURE_REUSE_MS: u64 = 10_000` and the field `recent_stale_failure: std::sync::Mutex<Option<(u64, Instant, String)>>` (generation, when, error reason).
  - Give `renew_with_fallback_since` a parameter `reuse_recent_failure: bool`. Pass true from `force_renewal_unless_replaced` and false from `force_renewal` and every other caller.
  - After taking `renew_gate`, and only when the generation is unchanged and the flag is true: if the stored entry matches `seen_generation` and is younger than RENEW_FAILURE_REUSE_MS, increment `tv_token_renew_failure_reused_total` and return `Err(ApplicationError::AuthenticationFailed { reason: stored.clone() })`. Same text, so classification and the page latch are identical.
  - On a fresh failure, store `(seen_generation, now, rendered reason)`.
  - Cold path only.
- 8c. In `force_renewal_unless_replaced`, reword the `error!` text and the `NotificationEvent::AuthenticationFailed` reason: "a Dhan live-feed connection was told its login is no longer valid (Dhan code 807, 808 or 809) and both the renewal and a fresh login failed (...)". Keep the latch (`stale_credential_failure_pages` / `take_stale_credential_page`) and the broker name.

STEP 9. Production closure (crates/app/src/dhan_feed_stack.rs, inside the single `run_connection_with_commands(` call, ~14950)
- The closure becomes `|request: TokenRefreshRequest| async move { ... }`, written with the move semantics the existing closure uses (an Arc clone of `dialled_generation`).
- Body:
  1. `let dialled = dialled_generation.load(Relaxed);`
  2. If `request.skip_if_presented == Some(dialled)`, return `TokenRefreshReport { presented: dialled, outcome: NotAttempted }` WITHOUT calling the manager.
  3. If there is no manager, return `{ presented: dialled, outcome: Failed }`.
  4. Otherwise `let res = manager.force_renewal_unless_replaced(dialled).await; let current = manager.renew_generation();`. Keep the R3 RENEW_FAILURES power-of-two `error!` on Err, and make its comment say "Post-807/808/809".
  5. The outcome is `Fresh { current }` if `current != dialled`, else `Deferred` if `res` is an Err that `is_deferred_renewal_failure` accepts, else `Failed`. That includes `Ok` with an unchanged generation, which cannot happen today but fails safe.
- Add a doc note on the closure: a depth-account socket must get its own closure that only re-reads its own SSM token (per 0a). There is no code for this today: no depth-account socket is dialled (Verified).
- The generation read order is unchanged: `feed_token_recording_generation` reads the generation before the token, so a recorded generation is never newer than the presented token. The safe direction is to refresh again rather than park.

STEP 10. Docs and alarm text
- deploy/aws/terraform/live-lane-alarms.tf: change only the `alarm_description` strings at ~160 (dhan-socket-parked) and ~382 (all sockets gone). "806/808/810" becomes "806/810, or an 808 that a refreshed token did not cure". Nothing else in either alarm changes.
- crates/common/src/error_code.rs: the doc on `AuthGapDisconnectTokenMap` (~148) gets a dated note matching 0e.
- crates/core/src/websocket/types.rs: add a one-line doc pointer on `is_reconnectable()` / `requires_token_refresh()` saying supervisor policy is `classify_disconnect`. Their behaviour is unchanged.

STEP 11. Error codes
- Every new line is `error!` with `code = ErrorCode::WsGapDisconnectClassification.code_str()` and a `stage` field from: refresh_then_redial, parked_fresh_token_rejected, parked_refresh_unavailable, parked_refresh_ceiling.
- No new ErrorCode variant.

Risk (Assumed, not measured): one socket's spurious 808 renews the account token. If RenewToken invalidates the token the other 15 healthy sockets hold, they each get 807 and reconnect, which is a tick gap. 809 already has the same single-socket exposure today (Verified: TokenStale arm). It is bounded to one renewal per generation by coalescing, to one renewal per 10 s on failure, and to 4 per 300 s per slot. Skipping renewal while siblings still deliver would need a shared per-generation delivery signal that does not exist. Recommend measuring auth_rejected against token_stale bursts after deploy.

After that the slot gets today's park and page. Failed renewals are shared for 10 s, so all slots together send about one RenewToken call per burst. result.summary:
The defect is real, and there are two parts (Verified on origin/main).

(1) `FRAME_SILENCE_REDIAL_SECS = 300` is one threshold for every socket kind. `ConnectionSupervisor::poll` never reads `slot.endpoint`. So a deaf main-feed or depth-20 socket stays blind for 5 minutes, and the deaf alarm pages at 600 s.

(2) The bigger problem: the same 300 s rule closes and redials HEALTHY but quiet depth-200 sockets. Each one carries a single contract, and the repo itself measured 56 minutes of benign silence on one (`worst_connection_tick_age_secs` excludes depth-200 for that reason). The watchdog test pins this redial: `a_ponging_socket_that_delivers_no_frame_is_redialled_after_the_frame_silence_window` uses Depth200 and expects a redial at 300 s.

The fix uses evidence instead of time alone.
- **Main feed and depth-20:** redial at 60 s / 90 s, but only when at least 2 OTHER sockets of the same kind delivered in the last 10 s. This applies only within 09:15–15:15 IST, only when the socket holds enough instruments, only with no 805 halt or overflow episode, and only with a per-kind spacing between such redials. The threshold escalates per socket on every redial that does not cure it. Otherwise the 300 s rule applies as today.
- **Depth-200:** a 900 s time backstop, plus a fast path. If the main feed shows its contract trading 30 s or more after the depth socket's last frame (taken from the read task, so it is immune to the depth shed), the socket is redialled.

The fast paths ship in SHADOW mode by default: they count "would redial" for a week before a one-line config flip to act. That makes the unmeasured gap figures measured before anything acts on them. The depth-200 change (fewer redials) is active from merge. The alarm stays at 600 s.

Review points folded in:
- Read-task wall-ms baseline. Both reviewers were right: the drain's stamp freezes during a depth shed.
- Escalation. R1 was right: the first frame after every dial resets `attempt`, so a deaf socket that bursts a snapshot after each dial loops every ~61 s and never reaches the flap ceiling.
- A dial-generation tag on the cross-feed request.
- `rotation_halted()` gating, with a `data_silence` refusal label.
- Publishing `depth200_held` at every place the guard changes.
- `slot_owner` instead of a new `SLOT_KIND`.
- Instrument-count floor.
- At least 2 siblings, to cover a stall of the F&O segment only.
- Spacing between fast redials pool-wide.
- Explicit evidence opt-in for test isolation.
- A noise-lock row recording how this interacts with the reconnect-slow and deaf alarms.

Dropped or changed:
- The design's 1,800 s depth-200 backstop: changed to 900 s. The 56-minute evidence is weaker than the design presented (it ran partly pre-open, under the old re-fit), and a deaf contract the main feed does not track needs recovery in under 30 minutes.
- R2's claim that every false redial pages reconnect-slow: kept only as a recorded interaction. A healthy main socket gets a frame pushed on subscribe (the code comment says the prev-close packet arrives before the ack), so its recovery sample is about 2 s. The alarm definition is unchanged.
- Separate per-segment sibling classes: replaced by the at-least-2-siblings rule. It covers the same failure without new state.

4. PURE DECISION
`pub const fn silence_redial_basis(endpoint, silent_secs, confirmed_threshold_secs, confirmed_window_open, overflow_or_halted, live_siblings, held, spacing_ok) -> Option<SilenceBasis>`:
- Depth200: `Backstop` if `silent >= 900`, else None (cross-feed arrives through its own event, §6).

- OrderUpdate: None.

- At the top of the Live branch in poll: if `strikes > 0` and `now - last_silence_redial_at >= SILENCE_STRIKE_RESET_SECS`, set `strikes = 0`.
- Poll, Live branch:
  - keep the hold-at-now when the gate is closed;
  - else compute `silent`;

**The defect is real, exactly as reported.** Checked in origin/main, crates/core/src/websocket/pool_supervisor.rs:
- The Disconnected arm (line 2903) calls overflow_episode_note_disconnect(code, now) and passes no slot.
- Once any 805 has happened (OVERFLOW_ENGAGED), every close with no code goes to OverflowEpisodes::on_bare_reset (lines 1823-1828). That feeds both episodes, and OverflowEpisode::on_bare_reset (lines 1603-1610) fails Probing/Resuming unconditionally with FailedBareReset.
- probes_started goes up at the grant (line 1655) and is never refunded. fail() (lines 1747-1765) moves to DownForSession once 3 main-feed probes (6 depth) are spent. After that, wait_for_overflow_grant returns None, so the parked sockets stay down for the session.
- The scope lock records this rule on purpose (full file, line 8544: "an 805 on ANY socket, or any socket closing with no code, inside a window"), and test_probe_fails_on_sibling_bare_reset_in_window (line 17496) pins it.
- Net effect: one unrelated blip burns one of only 3 probes.

**Fix.** A probe now fails only on one of these:
- an 805 anywhere;
- the probed socket closing with no code, or its own idle watchdog firing;
- no first frame in time;
- another socket's no-code close that is CORROBORATED as an eviction. That means either some other socket (not the closing one, not one that dropped in the same burst) BEGAN a dial in the last 20 s, or the dropped socket does not reconnect within 120 s.

So a lone sibling blip that reconnects cleanly no longer burns a probe. An eviction caused by the probe's own dial still fails at once, as today.

**Review points folded in:**
- Dials are attributed by time, using a per-slot BeginDial instant. This replaces the design's window-wide DIAL_GENERATION snapshot, which wrongly failed on two separate blips and on one flapping sibling. Reading BeginDial rather than DialSucceeded also closes the race where the evicted socket's close is processed before the evicting dial's bump.
- A sibling counts as healed at its own DialSucceeded, not at its first frame. A depth-200 contract can legitimately stay blank for minutes, and after 15:30 nothing ticks.
- Each suspect gets its own heal deadline.
- A suspect that parks for a reason other than 805 is dropped.
- The watched socket's IdleElapsed now fails the window.
- Non-failure outcomes log at warn!.
- The jitter figure is corrected to 625 ms (RECONNECT_DELAY_WITH_JITTER_MAX_MS).
- The thread race test is replaced by deterministic orderings.
- The false claim that DHAT already covers the supervisor is dropped (no dhat_*.rs references it) and replaced by a source pin.

**Review points dropped:**
- "release_next skips start_watch": wrong. Its grant path calls start_watch (line 1718). A debug_assert is added anyway.
- Adding a separate BeginDial attempt counter: superseded by the per-slot instants.

**Honest scope.** The fix helps when ONE socket (or one burst) drops while the probed socket stays up. A blip on the box's own network also drops the probed socket, and that still fails the probe, as the ask allows.

No page, alarm or Telegram change, so no noise-lock row. The scope lock needs a dated 2026-10-06 amendment, quoting the operator's 2026-10-06 approval.

Ship, but smaller than first asked. The order is: measure first (M0), then set the receive buffer size per socket (A), then lock the program's code pages in memory only if M0 shows the reader thread taking major page faults (B, conditional). Replacing the frame ring with a pre-allocated queue (C) is dropped; only a DHAT test is added that records the ring's current allocation behaviour.

**Is the defect real?** Yes, but the evidence is weaker than the original ask implies.
- The 371,828 memory-throttle events came from one incident on 2026-09-03: a 21 GB spill file read whole, since fixed to stream. Verified from the comments in tickvault.service and boot_helpers.rs.
- Whether the cgroup memory throttle still hits during a session is Unknown. `oom_monitor` parses only the `oom_kill` line (Verified), and nothing publishes the throttle count, memory pressure, or the reader thread's major faults.
- No code sets SO_RCVBUF. Verified: the dial goes through `connect_async_tls_with_config` at connection.rs:1874, and tokio-tungstenite 0.29 calls `TcpStream::connect` internally.
- The host is tuned: `rmem_max` is 128 MiB and `tcp_rmem` is `4096 1048576 134217728` with automatic sizing on (Verified, `99-tickvault-net.conf`). Each socket starts at 1 MiB and is only bounded per socket. That conf records the per-socket size as "unfixed (PR #1738)", and 26 × 128 MiB = 3.25 GiB is what holds the depth account OFF.
- Nothing locks memory pages (no mlock), and the host has no swap.
- The frame ring is a tokio mpsc. Under backlog it allocates a 32-slot block per 32 frames (tokio `block.rs` / `list.rs::reclaim_block`, Verified). Tungstenite already allocates on the same thread for every message, so the ring adds little.

**Review points folded in:**
1. Do not set SO_RCVBUF when `rmem_max` is below the request. Any user value locks the buffer and turns off automatic sizing, so an untuned host would end up with about 416 KiB instead of autotuning from 1 MiB.
2. Ban `client_async_tls_with_config(request, tcp, None` in the existing explicit-config test. Without it, that test passes vacuously after the change and tungstenite's default 64 MiB message ceiling could silently come back.
3. Fix the M0 thread-id source:
   - `on_thread_start` is installed only when `pin_core` is `Some` (Verified, reader_runtime.rs:386).
   - There can be up to `MAX_WS_READER_THREADS` = 4 workers.
   - The runtime can be disabled.
   - Fix: walk `/proc/self/task/*/comm` for the exact name `tv-ws-reader` and sum the faults. This needs no libc.
4. Do not put any file I/O or `mlock` in `reader_runtime.rs`. `hot_path_no_blocking_guard` scans that whole file and bans `std::fs::`, `File::open(` and `.lock()` (Verified).
5. The kernel-tuning guard must keep `rmem_max × N` as the bound it enforces, because the rollback path restores automatic sizing up to 128 MiB per socket. It must also record `tcp_mem`, which the conf leaves at the kernel default (Verified unset).
6. `majflt` is the 10th whitespace token after the last `)` in the stat line.
7. A missing PSI file reads as "unavailable", never as 0.
8. The doubling of the buffer value on read-back applies only on Linux.
9. Strip IPv6 brackets from the host and keep the old error text for an address that resolves to nothing.
10. Keep `count_dial_failure("connect")` for both TCP and TLS failures, so the metric's labels do not change.
11. The rollback test asserts the returned outcome, not a value read back from the kernel.
12. Roll back with an env var read in core. This keeps `crates/common` untouched and avoids workspace-wide test escalation.
13. B locks only the program's code (`r-xp`) mappings, including the dynamic loader. It lives in a new boot-only module in core and measures before it locks.
14. If C is ever built, the last `Sender`'s Drop must wake the receiver.

**Dropped or reworded:**
- "1 MiB ≈ one second of open-hour traffic" is withdrawn. The repo's own figures suggest about 4 s per main socket. The per-kind sizes are now labelled Assumed and are to be re-checked against the existing receive-queue max gauge.
- "The reader is exposed because tungstenite allocates on every frame" is withdrawn. A malloc that reuses freed heap charges no new memory to the cgroup. The real exposure is new-page faults and major faults on file-backed pages.
- A is no longer claimed to absorb memory-throttle stalls. While the cgroup reclaims memory, the kernel signals socket pressure and stops growing the TCP window whatever SO_RCVBUF says (Assumed kernel behaviour). A reliably helps only with CPU, scheduling or lock stalls and global `tcp_mem` pressure.
- The order-update socket's 128 MiB in the worst-case sum stays as a conservative bound. Whether that socket is spawned at all was not checked.

**Rules this respects:**
- No new or changed Telegram or CloudWatch page, so the noise-lock file needs no row.
- No subscribe, redial, `ROTATION_HALTED` or 805 path is touched.
- Open sockets pick up the new buffer size only on a genuine reconnect or a restart. A deliberate redial to apply it would be a REJECT under the 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02 scope-lock sections.
- Nothing is added per frame.

The defect is real, but the original ask blames the wrong sink. Verified: stdout is not registered in production. config/base.toml:475 sets log_to_stdout = false, and nothing in config/ or deploy/ overrides it. The false pages come from three other sinks:
- errors_log, which is always registered (main.rs ~1855, init_lossy_non_blocking).
- candles and live_ticks, registered at main.rs ~1945 with register_log_drop_counter(cat.prefix()). Both are TRACE-level sinks.

Verified: none of those three files is shipped. collect_list in deploy/aws/cloudwatch-agent.json holds only errors.jsonl.2* and app.2*, and the category files live in subdirectories that the app.2* glob does not reach. Yet the alarm tv-<env>-log-lines-dropped (data-at-risk-alarms.tf:201) reads tv_log_lines_dropped_total as a Sum on the host dimension only. So a drop in a file nobody reads in CloudWatch pages anyway. That also buries the one case the page exists for: a drop on app_log or errors_jsonl, which can hide a coded ERROR from its filter alarm.

Fix: use the house metrics-log filter with a label slice (the seal-drop / §2.10 route). One filter over /tickvault/<env>/metrics matches $.sink = app_log or errors_jsonl and writes a derived metric, tv_log_lines_dropped_shipped_total. The existing alarm switches to that metric. Its name, threshold, period, notBreaching, empty ok_actions, host-only dimension and Telegram line stay the same. No Rust production change is needed, because the boot seed already covers exactly the two sliced labels.

- Ship as three serial PRs so the page is never blind:

  - The operator then checks that the filter matches.
  - PR-2 switches the alarm.
  - PR-3 removes the raw name from the EMF selector, only after PR-2 is applied.
- The premise that the metrics log carries the label as a top-level sink field is NOT live-verified for any house slice. If it is wrong, the filter never matches and the page stays green forever. That failure is silent, not loud as the design said, which is why PR-2 waits on a measured match.

- The boot-seed label check needs its own parser for the `for sink in [..]` loop form, because zero_registered_names() reads names only.

The two reported sites (Verified):
- sandbox_window_boot (L740-749, OMS-GAP-06) is lost. Only std's bare 'Error: ...' reaches stderr, with no code.
- boot_replay_failed (L1288-1296, WS-SPILL-02) is lost, and boot carries on silently. It is worse than reported: ws_wal_replay_refused stays false, so the else arm at L3243-3256 runs confirm_replayed and archives earlier boots' staged segments unread. That arm's own comment admits it.

Other lines lost the same way (Verified):
- RESILIENCE-01 at L1127, then exit(1).
- The WsFrameSpill init failure at L1369, then exit(1). It also has no code.

1. Install the metrics recorder first, right after config extract. Its Result is kept and logged once the subscriber exists.
2. Install the subscriber and the panic hook before validate and before every boot step that logs.
3. Flush the log sinks before every exit that happens after the install.

- pub const LOG_SINK_FLUSH_BUDGET: Duration = Duration::from_millis(1_000).
- pub enum LogFlushOutcome { Flushed, TimedOut, NothingToFlush }.
- fn flush_guards(slot: &Mutex<Vec<WorkerGuard>>, budget: Duration) -> LogFlushOutcome:
  - Take the Vec; if it is empty, return NothingToFlush.
  - For each guard: put it in an Arc<Mutex<Option<WorkerGuard>>>, spawn a std thread named tv-log-flush that takes it, drops it, and sends on an mpsc channel.
